method: Independent clean-room audit of the complete exact runtime assignment on the frozen 1,782-file snapshot. Read all 109 handwritten assigned files in full: 46 runtime modules and 63 tests, fixtures and runtime documentation, including asynchronous ownership, activity/history gates, error delivery, process controllers and persistence paths. Read the current supporting method catalogs, core value/error contracts and receipt projection dependencies listed separately below. Reviewed the current pinned protocol contract and only the permitted current acceptance catalogue; no prior audit artifacts, sibling code or Git history were consulted. Reviewed .work/verify-protocol.mjs, executed the installed 0.164.0 CLI generation commands in fresh isolated homes, compared the exact full path sets and bytes of all 1,362 generated artifacts, then parsed all generated JSON/TS, validated JSON Schema meta-schemas, resolved every local schema reference and generated import, compared all four native method unions and checked 105 literal runtime schema names. Manually traced canonical timeline validation exceptions and native request/notification mappings. Reviewed tests for actual behavior, ownership changes, before-write races, unknown delivery, bounded resources and missing cases rather than treating passing assertions as correctness. Executed exactly three focused existing test files (38 assertions, zero skipped) for realtime/history/adapter behavior and one isolated deterministic current-module protocol-ordering repro. Reviewed initial helper errors, corrected only ignored audit helpers and retained the final results. No product source, tests, documentation or feature evidence was edited; no full suite, SSH, external model/MCP, live provider or personal configuration access occurred.

coverage.generatedInspection: Exact fresh regeneration and byte comparison plus complete-file JSON Schema / TS syntax, reference, import and method-union semantic scans; generated files were not represented as manually read prose.

reviewedBoundaries: Native line-framed RPC: Unicode validation, typed request IDs, shared serialized writer, retained-byte/pending budgets, native error preservation, prewrite versus postwrite timeout delivery and epoch closure.

Worker HTTP/WebSocket: token/socket authentication, fresh channel identities, lease admission captured before bodies, owner revocation before cleanup, final write fences and bounded private event routing.
Runtime work: per-thread concurrency, native status/goal/queue continuation, global configuration/CLI exclusions, stale read revisions, full combined turn/timeline proof and explicit resume only.

Private capabilities: device/OAuth handoffs, MCP streams/results, realtime inputs, prediction source tombstones, Guardian retry authority, owner and epoch expiry, redaction and durable receipt projection.

Native process resources: Windows suspended job assignment/kill-on-close and separate cleanup acknowledgement; Linux subreaper/pidfd descendants; terminal/controller result versus independently confirmed tree cleanup.

Persistent attachments and workspace results: immutable descriptor identities/digests, physical quota/tombstones, retained unknown pins, worker-owned witnesses, gateway/helper digests, exact source/operation versions and private worktree bindings.

Extension and environment adapters: explicit positive catalogs and authorization, versioned config writes, plugin materialization/share scopes, completed imports, remote executor registrations and inspected native cwd, provider capability checks.

User-visible error semantics: not_sent versus unknown, partial conversation identity, no replay, bounded incomplete history, unsupported forms, original diagnostic severity, terminal exit versus cleanup and private ephemeral result expiry.

validations.explanation: The byte-identical pinned generator emits three TS-only legacy client methods and two TS-only raw response notifications. The current runtime has no references to these five methods. They are recorded as upstream format asymmetry, not claimed as TS/JSON equality or a repository defect.

validations.mode: Current modules transformed into ignored temporary ESM files using Node stripTypeScriptTypes; no implementation substitutions or source edits. Host only supplies deterministic schema-valid events/acks.

findings.title: Fence prior realtime sessions before assigning thread-only notifications to a new owner
findings.trigger: Session A stops and receives the empty ThreadRealtimeStopResponse; the wrapper marks A closed and permits session B on the same thread. A valid late canonical item from A, explicitly carrying A realtimeSessionId, or a delayed thread-only close/SDP/audio event then arrives.
findings.impact: notification() selects B solely by threadId. It emits A transcript under B sessionHandle/clientId/eventChannelId without comparing the explicit item session ID. A delayed closed event also closes B and releases its activity barrier while B may still be running. The private per-connection voice ownership invariant and current-session state are therefore not preserved across same-thread reuse.
evidence: src/runtime/realtime.ts:64-76 generates a realtimeSessionId but does not retain it as the expected identity before startup notifications.
src/runtime/realtime.ts:104-110 selects the nonclosed session by threadId and forwards valid item notifications without checking item.realtimeSessionId; started can overwrite nativeSessionId.
src/runtime/realtime.ts:116 marks a session closed/reusable on the empty stop acknowledgement, independently of its closed notification.

protocol/ts/v2/ThreadRealtimeItem.ts carries realtimeSessionId; ThreadRealtimeClosedNotification, ThreadRealtimeSdpNotification and ThreadRealtimeOutputAudioDeltaNotification are thread-only and provide no session discriminator.

Deterministic current-module repro .work/round8/realtime-repro.mjs: start A, stop ack, start B, inject old canonical transcript and close. .work/round8/realtime-repro.json records the old session ID inside params while the envelope targets new-channel/new-owner/B handle, followed by B readback state closed.
The 38 existing realtime/timeline/service assertions pass, but none covers stop acknowledgement followed by another owner and late prior-session notification.
findings.recommendation: Retain the expected generated native session identity from admission and discard mismatched session-bearing notifications. Do not reuse a thread-only notification ownership slot until an explicit terminal/drain boundary is established; where the upstream contract cannot establish that boundary, retain a tombstone or require an epoch reset. Add regression coverage for delayed prior-session canonical items and close/SDP/audio events after same-thread restart.
findings.confidenceBoundary: The routing defect is reproduced using schema-valid deterministic events and current implementation modules. No real provider voice session was invoked, and this report does not claim observation of that event ordering from a live provider.

limitations: Complete here means complete assigned audit coverage, not a clean audit or comprehensive product validation. One actionable finding remains.
The full suite and post-gate acceptance runs were deliberately not invoked and are outside this audit; no pass result is claimed for them.

Real provider voice/audio, external model/MCP/OAuth/account/remote-control integrations were not invoked. The realtime finding is a deterministic valid-event ordering reproduction, not a measured provider event trace.
Linux/systemd/cross-UID and real Windows process-tree integration tests were statically reviewed but not executed in this audit. No prior README-linked acceptance evidence was opened or inherited.
Only the exact three named existing test files were run; remaining assigned tests/fixtures were read for contract and regression adequacy, not reported as executed.

Semantic helper preparation first failed because TypeScript 7 package root exposes no legacy compiler API; it was replaced with Node syntax parsing. Method extraction was then corrected for quoted property names and directory index imports. These were audit-helper issues only; final complete scan reports zero structural errors.
toolingNotes: Read installed TypeScript/Vite package metadata to select the available local parsing/transformation path. No dependencies were installed or changed.
No memory or old audit report was used. Current tests/runtime/README.md references historical evidence; those references were not opened or used as current proof.
